body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application. What is claimed is:

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A sensory mapping method for a human brain, the method comprising:flattening [[the]] acortical surface of the human brain to form a flattened cortical surface, the flattened cortical surface comprising a two-dimensional surface;
projecting functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMIRI) data onto the flattened cortical surface;
smoothing, by a smoothing process, the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, the smoothing process comprising:determining retinotopic coordinates of each of a plurality of cortical areas based on the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data and smoothing, by a diffeomorphic smoothing algorithm, the retinotopic coordinates of each of the plurality of cortical areas to form smoothed retinotopic coordinates of each of the plurality of cortical areas and repeating the diffeomorphic smoothing algorithm until a maximum absolute value of a Beltrami coefficient for the retinotopic coordinates of each of the plurality of cortical areas is less than one; and
responsive to the smoothing process, generating a diffeomorphic sensory map.
2.-5. (Cancelled)34
6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the flattening comprises:applying harmonic mapping to a unit disk; and
refining repetitively parametric coordinate for each point on a parameter domain to produce conformal mapping.
7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising rendering the diffeomorphic sensory map with an image of stimuli that activate the cortical surface.
8. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising registering a plurality of sensory maps across a plurality of subjects. different individuals.
9. (Cancelled)
10. (Original) The method of claim 8, wherein the registering is diffeomorphic.
11.-13. (Cancelled)1212
14. (Currently Amended) A sensory mapping method for a human brain, the method comprising:flattening [[the]] acortical surface of the human brain to form a flattened cortical surface, the flattened cortical surface comprising a two-dimensional surface;
projecting functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMIRI) data onto the flattened cortical surface to form a topology projection, the topology projection including a prior connectivity pattern of cortical surface areas;
processing the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)data to produce topological results, wherein the processing comprises:computing, by the topology projection, a diffeomorphic topological map by normalizing the topological map relative to a Beltrami coefficient segmenting the cortical surface of the human brain by preserving the prior connectivity pattern of cortical surface areas:
decoding the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data based on at least one topological condition within each cortical area on a vertex by vertex basis and repeating the segmentation and decoding until a theoretically guaranteed convergence occurs; and
responsive to the processing, generating a diffeomorphic sensory map.
15.-16. (Cancelled)
17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14, further comprising registering a plurality of sensory maps across a plurality of subjects. different individuals.
18. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the registering is diffeomorphic.
19. (Original) The method of claim 17, further comprising analyzing the plurality of sensory maps in a common space.
20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the registering comprises:applying the Beltrami coefficient to quantify diffeomorphism; and
modeling the registering in an optimization framework.
